_doc: Best known upper bounds for s(n), n = 1..324, taken as the SMALLER of two public catalogues, both retrieved 2026-11-11. (1) 'Squares in Squares' maintained by David Ellsworth, the successor of Erich Friedman's Packing Center page (https://erich-friedman.github.io/packing/squinsqu/ now redirects to it): https://kingbird.myphotos.cc/packing/squares_in_squares.html (HTTP Last-Modified 2026-09-24; cross-checked against https://kingbird.myphotos.cc/packing/squares_in_squares__triangular_table.html). It prints 14 decimals followed by an ellipsis (truncated). (2) The Squares Project frontier, https://jlevy.github.io/squares/frontier.html, whose per-n case records live at https://github.com/jlevy/squares/tree/main/packing/frontier (repo head 591644a9e9 (2026-11-11T11:02:26Z)); it supersedes (1) at many n with results from September-November 2026. 'upper' is copied digit for digit from whichever source is lower; 'upper_kingbird' and 'upper_squares_project' keep both. upper_truncated_down is deliberately NOT set anywhere, so verify.py subtracts half a unit in the last printed place before comparing (conservative). proven_optimal is true if either source lists a proof, including proofs only reported. Lower bounds: Friedman, 'Packing Unit Squares in Squares: A Survey and New Results', EJC DS7 (2009), Table 2 (https://erich-friedman.github.io/papers/squares/squares.html); the Squares Project's verified lower bounds; optimality proofs; all extended by monotonicity and the area bound. POST-RUN CORRECTION (2026-11-11, after the run had ended): a third public source was added, (3) the Kaggle 'Squares in Squares' per-puzzle leaderboard, https://www.kaggle.com/code/inversion/squares-in-squares-per-puzzle-leaderboard (notebook version 28; newest submission in the table 2026-11-08 04:29:46 UTC; retrieved 2026-11-11 22:06 UTC), which lists the smallest side accepted by the competition's grader for each n, side only, with no packing. Every entry carries it in 'upper_kaggle_per_puzzle'. Where a team's side is smaller than both catalogues, 'upper' and 'source' now hold the Kaggle value, copied digit for digit (50 decimals), and 'upper_catalogues' / 'source_catalogues' keep what the two catalogues say. So 'upper' is the SMALLEST of three public sources. See search/add_kaggle_source.py.
